class.name: RockGenerator
class.brief_description: Makes rocks and stones as real geometry: broken along the joints of a rock type, rounded by transport, weathered.
class.description: Each rock is a block cut by the joint planes of its rock type (near-cuboid, as natural fragments are: Domokos et al. 2020), with secondary fractures, impact chips and partial cracks, held as a signed distance field. Transport rounds it by Bloore's abrasion flow (the surface moves in at [code]1 + c * curvature[/code]: corners first, then slow shrinking; Domokos et al. 2014), for [member transport_distance] metres of river against the rock type's abrasion length. Weathering by rock type is carved in: spheroidal rounding of granite and basalt, solution pits on limestone tops, sandstone laminae and tafoni, basalt vesicles, slate cleavage steps, glacial striations. Surface nets make the mesh, meshoptimizer its LODs. The mesh rests on its flattest side (local Y the short axis, X the long one) and its b axis is 2 units long. See docs/ideas/rocks.md.

method.name: generate
method.description: Makes one rock for the current [member seed]. Its metadata: [code]rock_axes[/code] (half lengths along x, y, z: long, short and intermediate axis), [code]rock_bottom[/code] (lowest y), [code]rock_hull[/code] (up to 48 points for a convex collision shape), [code]rock_faces[/code] (the planes it broke along), [code]rock_roundness[/code], [code skip-lint]rock_type[/code] and [code]rock_family[/code]. The mesh rests on its flattest side and its b axis is 2 units long, so an instance scaled by [code]s[/code] is a stone of b-axis diameter [code]2 s[/code].

method.name: generate_library
method.description: Makes [param count] rocks from seeds [member seed] to [code]seed + count - 1[/code] on worker threads.

method.name: get_last_build_msec
method.description: Milliseconds the last [method generate] or [method generate_library] took.

method.name: get_last_triangle_count
method.description: Triangles in the most detailed level of the last rock, or of all rocks of the last library.

method.name: get_material
method.description: The shared material of a rock type: mineral colour and specks, bands, weathered rind, lichen and moss, a ground contact band, the water film and the weather wetness and snow.

method.name: get_roundness
method.description: Roundness reached by [member transport_distance] for this rock type, from 0 (fresh) to 1 (fully rounded), from the rock type's abrasion length.

method.name: get_shader_code
method.description: The source of the rock shader used by [method get_material].

members.member: Scales the grid resolution of the shape. Lower is faster and coarser.

What made the rock: fresh rockfall, scree, glacial boulder, river cobble, beach pebble or cliff block. Sets the size of the block, how much it is chipped, rounded and flattened, and the default resolution.
Builds distance levels of detail for the mesh.
Grid cells across the rock. [code]0[/code] uses the family's own resolution.
The rock: how it is jointed and breaks, how fast it abrades, how it weathers and its colour.
Seed of the rock. Each seed gives a different rock of the same type and family.
Collapses edges of the most detailed level only where neither the surface nor its normal moves visibly, which keeps every chip, pit and groove with fewer triangles.
Metres the rock travelled before it came to rest, which rounds it by Bloore abrasion: corners first, then slow shrinking. Below 0 uses the family's own distance.
Strength of weathering in place, from 0 to 1: spheroidal rounding, solution pits, laminae, tafoni. Below 0 uses the family's own.

constants.constant: Massive crystalline rock: few joints, spheroidal weathering, grey with dark and light specks.
Bedded and laminated, warm, wears fastest, with tafoni hollows.
Dark, in five to seven-sided columns, with vesicles.
Dark grey, splits in thin cleavage plates.
Fresh blocks fallen from a cliff.
Smaller fresh stones on talus, chipped on the way down.
Subrounded boulders out of till, with a striated facet.
Beach stones, rounded and flattened by the swash.
Large jointed blocks set into cliff faces.
